notable_absence.finding: The page names the internal caller (cluster manager / ns_server) and the mechanism (DCP) but never states which DCP stream state(s) from cbstats-dcp.md's enum (takeover-send, takeover-wait) this command's vb/name pair actually reads - the 'For internal use only' framing and the options table (just vb and name) give a reader no way to connect this command's output to the stream lifecycle documented on the sibling page.

cross_component_finding: This page is one of exactly two commands in the batch (with cbstats-tap-vbtakeover.md) that explicitly names its internal caller - 'This command is used by cluster manager (ns_server) to track the progress of rebalance using DCP' - rather than leaving the consumer of its statistics unstated, as cbstats-dcp.md, cbstats-dcpagg.md, cbstats-checkpoint.md, cbstats-durability-monitor.md, cbstats-failovers.md and cbstats-warmup.md all do. This is the batch's clearest authorship-provenance signal: cbstats is mostly an administrator-facing diagnostic surface with no stated consumer, but for vBucket takeover specifically the docs name ns_server as the actual internal owner of the mechanism, with cbstats merely exposing its progress.
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - internal rebalance orchestration (ns_server) is Couchbase Server-specific machinery with no stated Capella or Sync Gateway analog on this page.
